summary: Fortune's review of the Fifth Third 1.67% Cash/Back Card, a no-annual-fee card with a flat, uncapped 1.67% return on all purchases and simple redemption by statement credit or direct deposit. It has no welcome bonus or bonus categories, and only existing Fifth Third checking or savings customers can qualify. The review compares it with the Capital One Quicksilver (1.5%) and Citi Double Cash (2%) and concludes it suits people who value simplicity.
one_line: Fortune reviews the Fifth Third 1.67% Cash/Back Card, a simple no-annual-fee flat-rate card open only to existing Fifth Third bank customers.
key_facts: The Fifth Third 1.67% Cash/Back Card earns an unlimited, flat 1.67% on all purchases; the rate ties to the bank's name (5/3 = 1.67).
The card has a $0 annual fee and a $0 foreign transaction fee.
Purchase APR is 20.74%–29.99% variable; there is a 0% intro APR on balance transfers for the first 12 billing cycles, and the balance transfer fee is $5 or 4%, whichever is greater.
The cash advance APR is 29.99% plus $10 or 5% of the advance, whichever is greater; the late payment fee is up to $40 and the minimum interest charged is $1.50.
You must have a Fifth Third checking or savings account to qualify for the card.
The card has no welcome bonus and no bonus spending categories.
Rewards points are worth 1 cent each and are rounded to the nearest whole number; spending $6 earns 10.02 points, rounded to 10.
Rewards can be redeemed as a statement credit or a direct deposit into a Fifth Third account with no minimum threshold, or through monthly auto-redemption.
Cell phone protection pays up to $800 per claim (max two claims or $1,000 per 12 months) with a $50 deductible when the monthly phone bill is paid with the card.
The card works with Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay, and the Fifth Third mobile app lets users lock and unlock the card; Mastercard ID Theft Protection is included.
The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards card earns 1.5% unlimited, plus 5% on hotels and rental cars via Capital One Travel and $200 after spending $500 in the first 3 months.
The Citi Double Cash Card effectively earns 2% (1% on purchase, 1% on payment) but has no welcome bonus, charges foreign transaction fees and lacks cell phone insurance.
Fifth Third operates primarily in the Midwest, with branches from Illinois to West Virginia to Florida.
Cardholders should use the card at least once every six months to avoid closure for inactivity.
